aboutPageContent.intro: Women’s empowerment is central to true social change.

whoWeAre.title: Who we are
paragraphs: Rangbheeni is a women-led grassroot initiative working at the intersection of sustainability, livelihoods, and social equity rooted in the belief that those most affected by social and environmental challenges must be at the centre of the solutions.
Our work is not built for communities, but with them. Women from marginalized backgrounds are not just artisans, they are co-creators, decision-makers, and leaders shaping Rangbheeni every day.

Our grassroots programmes work in partnership with local communities to resolve the global skills gap and promote sustainable economic uplift. We believe that this work contributes to creating a more just, equitable, and sustainable world for everyone.
What makes Rangbheeni different is not just what we do, but how we do it, through trust, long-term engagement, and deep listening at the grassroots level.
whoWeAre.mission: To transform textile waste into sustainable solutions by empowering marginalised women with dignified livelihoods and supporting better educational opportunities for their children, ensuring those most affected by climate change become agents of change.
whoWeAre.vision: A sustainable world where waste is reimagined as a resource, women lead inclusive climate action, and every child has the opportunity to learn and flourish.

founder.name: Kumkum Masatkar
founder.title: Founder and President, Rangbheeni
paragraphs: With over 9 years of experience in the social sector, Kumkum has worked at both grassroots and administrative levels with women, transgender communities, and marginalized groups across urban and rural India. She holds a Master’s degree in Community Organisation and Development Practices from TISS Mumbai, where her work focused on gender, health, livelihoods, and labour rights.
Kumkum’s field experience revealed that many marginalized women possess valuable skills but lack consistent livelihood opportunities, keeping them financially dependent and socially restricted
This insight led her to found Rangbheeni in April 2024, an upcycling-based textile enterprise that creates sustainable livelihoods for marginalized women while addressing textile waste.

journeyPageContent.intro: The people most affected by textile waste and climate change should be at the center of the solution.

origin.title: How it started
paragraphs: Rangbheeni emerged from ground-level engagement, research, and continuous dialogue with the community.

Through this process, two interconnected challenges became clear:- limited livelihood opportunities for women and the growing issue of textile waste. While many women possessed skills like stitching and embroidery, there were no sustainable avenues to turn these into income. At the same time, discarded textiles were contributing to environmental damage, disproportionately affecting these communities.

Recognising this intersection, Rangbheeni was built to address both challenges together by transforming textile waste into sustainable products while creating dignified livelihood opportunities for women
What began with small conversations and trust-building has grown into a community-led effort focused on sustainability, resilience, and long-term change.

stories.title: Rescuing Women in Crisis
stories.excerpt: Rangbheeni rescued Meera from a harmful situation and supported her with legal aid and safe shelter.

sections.text: Rangbheeni works at the intersection of textile waste, climate justice, and social equity—transforming discarded materials into products and opportunity.
Women are trained in upcycling skills, quality finishing, and production practices that translate into stable work.
When communities most affected by climate change lead the solution, impact becomes sustainable.
Each product represents reclaimed value—of textile, of labor, and of future possibilities for children’s education.

stories.title: From Struggle to Self-Reliance
stories.excerpt: Rangbheeni helped Anita start her tailoring business. Today, she not only supports her family but also trains 10 other women.

sections.text: Collection drives help divert usable textiles from dumping and burning while creating material for upcycling.
Sorting and selection are done carefully—quality and durability matter for the final product.
Waste is not the end of a story—sometimes it’s the beginning.
The drive also becomes a community education moment—people see the value of circular choices.

stories.title: Creating Opportunities
stories.excerpt: Over 200 women have been provided employment opportunities in sustainable livelihood programs, building pathways for financial independence and dignity.

sections.text: Rangbheeni conducts sustainability and DIY upcycling workshops for institutions and corporates.
Participants learn practical ways to rethink textile waste while engaging with the idea of women-led climate action.
Sustainability becomes real when people can make something with their own hands.

stories.title: Training day: from basics to finish
stories.excerpt: A look inside a Rangbheeni upskilling session—from measurements and cutting to finishing and quality checks.

sections.text: Skill development starts with fundamentals—tools, safety, stitching basics, and consistent practice.
Over time, the group moves into finishing standards: strong seams, clean edges, and durable construction.
Dignity comes from skill—and skill comes from showing up, again and again.
Every session strengthens confidence, teamwork, and the ability to produce consistent work with pride.

stories.title: From sarees to usable everyday products
stories.excerpt: How pre-loved textiles are selected, prepared, and transformed into products designed for everyday use.

sections.text: Not every fabric is suitable for upcycling. We sort textiles by strength, feel, and longevity.
Preparation includes cleaning, reinforcement where needed, and design planning to reduce waste in cutting.
Circularity is not just reuse—it’s thoughtful design and long life.
The goal is simple: make products that last, and livelihoods that do too.

stories.title: Exhibitions and Tier 2 city reach
stories.excerpt: Taking women-led circular products to new audiences through exhibitions across Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities.

sections.text: Exhibitions are more than sales—they are awareness moments that help people connect climate choices to community outcomes.
Each event is also feedback: what customers use, what they value, and what designs are most practical.
Visibility builds confidence—when people see the work, they respect the craft.
Over time, this builds market access and helps women earn more predictable income from skilled work.

stories.title: Corporate gifting with a climate story
stories.excerpt: Why meaningful gifting can be climate-conscious—and how upcycled products carry both purpose and proof.

sections.text: Corporate gifting can become a sustainability touchpoint—when gifts are useful, durable, and rooted in circular production.
Rangbheeni collaborations support women-led livelihoods while diverting textile waste from dumping and burning.
A gift can carry a story—not just a logo.
We support bulk gifting and event collaborations with clear impact framing that partners can stand behind.

stories.title: Education support: what stable income makes possible
stories.excerpt: When livelihoods stabilize, families can plan—and children’s education becomes more secure and consistent.

sections.text: Livelihoods are not only about income—they’re about predictability, choice, and dignity.
As women earn more reliably through skilled work, families can prioritize school expenses and reduce interruptions.
Intergenerational change begins when a household can plan for tomorrow.
Rangbheeni’s model is built to support both climate resilience and long-term opportunity.
